questions.a: B) Insulin. Insulin causes cells to take up glucose and the liver to store it as glycogen.

questions.q: A reflex arc passes through the...
Impulses cross a synapse by a...
Name the organ that makes insulin.
TIR needs i greater than the...
Explain two effects of adrenaline and how they help in danger.
questions.a: Increases heart rate (1), delivering more oxygen and glucose to muscles (1); converts glycogen to glucose in liver (1), more glucose for respiration in muscles (1)
questions.model: Effect then benefit. Heart rate up: more blood with oxygen to muscles. Glucose released: fuel for respiration. Both mean more energy for action.

questions.q: Name the gland that secretes adrenaline.
Give one difference between nervous and hormonal responses.
questions.a: Hormonal is slower (or longer-lasting, chemical, widespread)

questions.q: A person eats a large meal. Describe how insulin returns their blood glucose to normal, and explain why this is an example of hormonal control. Portal response box.
questions.a: Blood glucose rises (1); detected by the pancreas (1); insulin secreted into the blood (1); carried to liver/muscles (1); glucose converted to glycogen/taken into cells, so level falls (1); chemical messenger carried in blood to a target organ (1)
questions.model: Teacher writes the first point: 'After the meal, glucose is absorbed and blood glucose rises.'

questions.q: Compare the speed of response to touching a hot object and to a rise in blood glucose.
questions.a: Touching heat: nervous, milliseconds (1); glucose: hormonal, minutes to hours (1)

questions.q: Why do people with type 1 diabetes check blood glucose before meals?
questions.a: They must inject the right amount of insulin because their pancreas does not make it.
